incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'g4p-prod-eu' at 96% GPU_util for the last 3m. Autoscaler delayed due to quota check. Paging SRE Oncall. Links: https://runbooks/redwood/incidents/1872345678
SRE Oncall: ack — I'm on it, grabbing logs and looking at autoscaler metrics.
Ravi: Are we seeing preemptions or just long queues?
SRE Oncall: No preemptions. High enqueue rates + several long-running low-priority batches from batch-worker-3. Queue depth spiked.
Marta: Noted. Which customers affected? Any external 5xx?
SRE Oncall: No 5xx. Increased tail latency for small-gen requests (~1.2s -> 2.8s). A few timeouts reported from internal heartbeat checks. Rerouting hasn't kicked in because pool still reports capacity.
Lauren: I'm going to throttle non-essential internal jobs (batch-worker-3). Will patch scaling config to be more aggressive for `low-latency` routes.
EngInfra: Patch ready. Pushing a temporary policy: reduce batch size for background jobs and increase min-replicas for `low-latency` class by 1.
Dave: FYI we've got spare capacity in us-west-2. Can we failover some traffic?
SRE Oncall: Prefer to avoid region failover unless forced — that adds latency for EU customers. First try quick local mitigations.
Ravi: If autoscaler quota check is the blocker, could be the API rate limit to cloud provider. I'll open a ticket but meanwhile we can bump the local desired count manually.
Marta: Agreed. Manual scale to +2 nodes for pool 'g4p-prod-eu' now?
SRE Oncall: Doing `kubectl scale --replicas=+2 deployment/g4p-pool-eu` and updating autoscaler guardrails.
SRE Oncall: (code)
```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/g4p-pool-eu --replicas=12
kubectl -n inference patch hpa/g4p-pool-eu -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":10}}'
```
SRE Oncall: Scaled. Queue depth decreasing, latency trending down.
Lauren: Throttled batch-worker-3 and 4, reduced batch_size from 256 -> 64.
Product Ops: Noting: no external customer tickets yet, but internal alerts flagged user-facing slowness for two accounts — cc @account-managers.
EngInfra: We're seeing the autoscaler API calls failing with 429 from provider for the quota-check endpoint. That explains delayed autoscale. Raising follow-up with cloud infra to increase API rate limit.
Dave: For remediation, recommend: 1) Fix autoscaler retry logic + backoff, 2) Add local fallback to increase minReplicas if queue depth > threshold, 3) Add circuit to demote low-priority batches, 4) Run capacity drills for EU pool.
Ravi: I'll own #1 and #2. ETA EOD tomorrow for PRs.
Marta: I'll own #3 (batch demotion) and schedule a runbook update. ETA 2d.
Lauren: I'll schedule capacity drill with infra — aim for next Tuesday 09:00 UTC.
Product Ops: I'll draft a short customer-facing note in case we need to communicate; tentatively hold until postmortem.
SRE Oncall: Marking incident as mitigated — queue depth normal, no timeouts. Leaving post-incident review to be scheduled. Good job team. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 (mitigated). Postmortem meeting suggested: 1872352000 (approx 1h from now). Use channel #postmortems and tag owners.
Ravi: If postmortem is in 1h I'll join. Also adding action items to issue tracker: INF-4923 (autoscaler backoff), INF-4924 (local minReplicas fallback), INF-4925 (batch demotion policy).
Marta: Adding runbook note: on scaling failure, manual scale + throttle background work. I'll drop a short snippet into docs.
Lauren: I'll create a small dashboard panel for autoscaler 429 rate and queue-depth-to-latency correlation.
Dave: Recommend flagging this for Dedicated customers — potential for similar behavior in reserved pools.
Product Ops: Noted. We'll review messaging after postmortem.
SRE Oncall: Final check — any outstanding customer impact or open pages?
Ravi: None from infra side.
Marta: None.
Lauren: None.
SRE Oncall: Closing thread. Postmortem invite will include link to logs + timeline + owners.
incident-bot: Postmortem scheduled: 1872352000. Meeting link: https://meet/redwood/1872352000. Action items: INF-4923 (Ravi), INF-4924 (Ravi), INF-4925 (Marta), DRILL-108 (Lauren).
